ştir, aslı sığınak anlamındaki asrdır, source:"ع ص ر,B011"}. Savaşta insanı saran zırhlar da bu köktendir: {ar:المعاصر الدروع مأخوذ من العصر لأنه يعصر بها, tr:el-meâsiru'd-durû', gloss:meâsir zırhlardır; insan onlarla korunduğu için asrdan alınmıştır, source:"ع ص ر,B016"}.

[¶18] Aynı kelimenin hem sıkıştırmayı hem sığınağı adlandırması ilk bakışta çelişki gibi görünür, ama ikisi de bir kavrayıştır. Sıkma bir şeyi dışarıdan sarar; sığınan ise kendisi bir şeyi sıkıca kavrar, zırh da bedeni dışarıdan sarar ve korur. Sıkışmış olan, bunalmış olan sığınağa koşar: deyimdeki sığınak tam da bunalmış kişinin sığınağıdır. Bu imge zamanın yanında duyulunca yemin edilen vakit hem insanı sıkıştıran bir süre hem de sığınılacak bir yer olarak görünür.

[¶19] Kur'an bir sığınağın zamanı nasıl kapattığını bir mağara hikâyesinde gösterir. Allah Peygamber'e, kavimlerinin taptıklarından ayrılan birkaç gencin haberini anlatır; onlar birbirine şöyle der: {ar:وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأْوُۥٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ يَنشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِۦ, tr:ve izi'tezeltumûhum ve mâ ya'budûne illallâhe fe'vû ile'l-kehfi yenşur lekum rabbukum min rahmetih, gloss:madem onlardan ve Allah'tan başka taptıklarından ayrıldınız, mağaraya sığının ki Rabbiniz rahmetinden size yaysın, source:18:16}. Sığındıklarında dua ederler: {ar:إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةًۭ, tr:iz eve'l-fityetu ile'l-kehfi fe-kâlû rabbenâ âtinâ min ledunke rahmeh, gloss:o gençler mağaraya sığınıp Rabbimiz, katından bize rahmet ver dediklerinde, source:18:10}. Sığınağın içinde zaman kapanır: {ar:فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ فِى ٱلْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدًۭا, tr:fe-darabnâ alâ âzânihim fi'l-kehfi sinîne adedâ, gloss:mağarada nice yıllar kulaklarının üstüne perde vurduk, source:18:11}. Uyandıklarında birbirlerine ne kadar kaldıklarını sorarlar ve cevapları {ar:لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍۢ, tr:lebisnâ yevmen ev ba'da yevm, gloss:bir gün ya da günün bir kısmı kaldık, source:18:19} olur; oysa {ar:وَلَبِثُوا۟ فِى كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلَٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍۢ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًۭا, tr:ve lebisû fî kehfihim selâse mietin sinîne vezdâdû tis'â, gloss:mağaralarında üç yüz yıl kaldılar, dokuz da eklediler, source:18:25}. Bu hikâyede asrın üç yüzü bir arada görünür, ama kelimenin kendisi geçmez: sığınak, uzun bir çağ ve uyuyanın bir an sandığı süre. Üçüncü ayette istisna edilen iman edenler bu sığınak imgesine yaslanır; kayıptan kurtuluş, bu sahnede bir yere sığınmak olarak duyulur.

## Kasırga ve kokunun yükselişi

[¶20] Kökün bir dalı göğe yükselen bir rüzgârı adlandırır. Rüzgâr yerden eser, tozu kaldırır ve onu sütun gibi göğe diker: {ar:الإعصار ريح تهب تثير الغبار فيرتفع إلى السماء كأنه عمود, tr:el-i'sâru rîhun tehubbu tusîru'l-gubâra fe-yertefi'u ile's-semâi keennehû amûd, gloss:i'sâr, esip tozu kaldıran ve onu sütun gibi göğe yükselten rüzgârdır, source:"ع ص ر,B004"}; dönerek yükselen tozun kendisine de {ar:الإعصار الغبار الذي يسطع مستديرا والجمع الأعاصير, tr:el-i'sâru'l-gubâru'llezî yesta'u mustedîrâ, gloss:i'sâr, dönerek yükselen tozdur, çoğulu eâsîr, source:"ع ص ر,B004"} denir. Bu rüzgârın işi, yerdeki şeyi döndürerek bir araya toplamak ve onu dik bir sütun hâlinde yukarı çekmektir. Aynı dal hoş bir şeyi de böyle anlatır: güzel kokular sürünmüş bir kadın geçtiğinde {ar:مرت امرأة متطيبة لذيلها عصر, tr:merrat imraetun mutetayyibetun li-zeylihâ asr, gloss:güzel koku sürünmüş bir kadın geçti, eteğinin ardından koku yükseliyordu, source:"ع ص ر,B004"} derlerdi; {ar:تكون العصرة من فوح الطيب وهيجه, tr:tekûnu'l-usratu min fevhi't-tîbi ve heycih, gloss:usra, kokunun yayılıp kabarmasıdır, source:"ع ص ر,B004"}. Hareket eden bir şeyin ardından kabarıp yükselen ya tozdur ya kokudur.

[¶21] Kur'an bu rüzgârı, yaşlılığın içine yerleştirilmiş bir bahçe misalinde anar. Allah Allah yolunda harcamaya dair misaller verir: gösteriş için harcayanın hâli üzerinde toprak bulunan düz bir kayadır, sağanak vurunca çıplak kalır {ar:فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌۭ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلٌۭ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلْدًۭا, tr:fe-meseluhû ke-meseli safvânin aleyhi turâbun fe-esâbehû vâbilun fe-terakehû saldâ, gloss:onun misali, üstünde toprak olan düz bir kaya gibidir; sağanak vurdu, onu çıplak bıraktı, source:2:264}; Allah'ın rızası için harcayanınki ise sağanak da çisenti de alsa iki kat ürün veren tepedeki bir bahçedir {source:2:265}. Sonra bir soru gelir: {ar:أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُۥ جَنَّةٌۭ مِّن نَّخِيلٍۢ وَأَعْنَابٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ, tr:e-yeveddu ehadukum en tekûne lehû cennetun min nahîlin ve a'nâbin tecrî min tahtihe'l-enhâr, gloss:biriniz, altından ırmaklar akan, hurmalık ve üzüm bağından bir bahçesi olmasını ister mi, source:2:266}; aynı ayette {ar:وَأَصَابَهُ ٱلْكِبَرُ وَلَهُۥ ذُرِّيَّةٌۭ ضُعَفَآءُ فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌۭ فِيهِ نَارٌۭ فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ, tr:ve esâbehu'l-kiberu ve lehû zurriyyetun duafâu fe-esâbehâ i'sârun fîhi nârun fahtarakat, gloss:kendisine yaşlılık çökmüş, zayıf çocukları varken, bahçeye içinde ateş olan bir kasırga isabet etsin de yansın, source:2:266}. Ayet kendi işini de söyler: {ar:كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ, tr:kezâlike yubeyyinullâhu lekumu'l-âyâti leallekum tetefekkerûn, gloss:Allah size ayetleri böyle açıklar ki düşünesiniz, source:2:266}.

[¶22] Bu bahçede kökün birkaç anlamı aynı yerde durur, ama kelime olarak yalnızca kasırga geçer. Bahçede üzüm vardır, yani sıkılacak meyve; ırmaklar ve bütün ürünler, yani gelir; sahibine yaşlılık gelmiştir, yani ömrün akşamüstü; ve bütün bunları, yerden kaldırdığını göğe diken, içinde ateş taşıyan bir rüzgâr yok eder. Bir ömür boyunca sıkılmayı bekleyen ürün, tam sahibinin yeniden ekecek gücü kalmadığı vakitte gider. İkinci ayetteki kaybın en somut resmi budur; kasırga, asrın yanında duyulduğunda zamanın biriktirdiğini bir anda savurabilen yüzüdür. Kokunun yükselişi ise aynı hareketin öteki ucunda durur: geçen birinin ardından toz değil, güzel bir iz kalabilir.

<<end of 103:1 reading, paragraphs numbered>>

Bu imge zamanın yanında duyulunca yemin edilen vakit hem insanı sıkıştıran bir süre hem de sığınılacak bir yer olarak görünür.

[¶19] Kur'an bir sığınağın zamanı nasıl kapattığını bir mağara hikâyesinde gösterir. Allah Peygamber'e, kavimlerinin taptıklarından ayrılan birkaç gencin haberini anlatır; onlar birbirine şöyle der: {ar:وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأْوُۥٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ يَنشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِۦ, tr:ve izi'tezeltumûhum ve mâ ya'budûne illallâhe fe'vû ile'l-kehfi yenşur lekum rabbukum min rahmetih, gloss:madem onlardan ve Allah'tan başka taptıklarından ayrıldınız, mağaraya sığının ki Rabbiniz rahmetinden size yaysın, source:18:16}. Sığındıklarında dua ederler: {ar:إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةًۭ, tr:iz eve'l-fityetu ile'l-kehfi fe-kâlû rabbenâ âtinâ min ledunke rahmeh, gloss:o gençler mağaraya sığınıp Rabbimiz, katından bize rahmet ver dediklerinde, source:18:10}. Sığınağın içinde zaman kapanır: {ar:فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ فِى ٱلْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدًۭا, tr:fe-darabnâ alâ âzânihim fi'l-kehfi sinîne adedâ, gloss:mağarada nice yıllar kulaklarının üstüne perde vurduk, source:18:11}. Uyandıklarında birbirlerine ne kadar kaldıklarını sorarlar ve cevapları {ar:لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍۢ, tr:lebisnâ yevmen ev ba'da yevm, gloss:bir gün ya da günün bir kısmı kaldık, source:18:19} olur; oysa {ar:وَلَبِثُوا۟ فِى كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلَٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍۢ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًۭا, tr:ve lebisû fî kehfihim selâse mietin sinîne vezdâdû tis'â, gloss:mağaralarında üç yüz yıl kaldılar, dokuz da eklediler, source:18:25}. Bu hikâyede asrın üç yüzü bir arada görünür, ama kelimenin kendisi geçmez: sığınak, uzun bir çağ ve uyuyanın bir an sandığı süre. Üçüncü ayette istisna edilen iman edenler bu sığınak imgesine yaslanır; kayıptan kurtuluş, bu sahnede bir yere sığınmak olarak duyulur.

## Kasırga ve kokunun yükselişi

[¶20] Kökün bir dalı göğe yükselen bir rüzgârı adlandırır. Rüzgâr yerden eser, tozu kaldırır ve onu sütun gibi göğe diker: {ar:الإعصار ريح تهب تثير الغبار فيرتفع إلى السماء كأنه عمود, tr:el-i'sâru rîhun tehubbu tusîru'l-gubâra fe-yertefi'u ile's-semâi keennehû amûd, gloss:i'sâr, esip tozu kaldıran ve onu sütun gibi göğe yükselten rüzgârdır, source:"ع ص ر,B004"}; dönerek yükselen tozun kendisine de {ar:الإعصار الغبار الذي يسطع مستديرا والجمع الأعاصير, tr:el-i'sâru'l-gubâru'llezî yesta'u mustedîrâ, gloss:i'sâr, dönerek yükselen tozdur, çoğulu eâsîr, source:"ع ص ر,B004"} denir. Bu rüzgârın işi, yerdeki şeyi döndürerek bir araya toplamak ve onu dik bir sütun hâlinde yukarı çekmektir. Aynı dal hoş bir şeyi de böyle anlatır: güzel kokular sürünmüş bir kadın geçtiğinde {ar:مرت امرأة متطيبة لذيلها عصر, tr:merrat imraetun mutetayyibetun li-zeylihâ asr, gloss:güzel koku sürünmüş bir kadın geçti, eteğinin ardından koku yükseliyordu, source:"ع ص ر,B004"} derlerdi; {ar:تكون العصرة من فوح الطيب وهيجه, tr:tekûnu'l-usratu min fevhi't-tîbi ve heycih, gloss:usra, kokunun yayılıp kabarmasıdır, source:"ع ص ر,B004"}. Hareket eden bir şeyin ardından kabarıp yükselen ya tozdur ya kokudur.

[¶21] Kur'an bu rüzgârı, yaşlılığın içine yerleştirilmiş bir bahçe misalinde anar. Allah Allah yolunda harcamaya dair misaller verir: gösteriş için harcayanın hâli üzerinde toprak bulunan düz bir kayadır, sağanak vurunca çıplak kalır {ar:فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌۭ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلٌۭ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلْدًۭا, tr:fe-meseluhû ke-meseli safvânin aleyhi turâbun fe-esâbehû vâbilun fe-terakehû saldâ, gloss:onun misali, üstünde toprak olan düz bir kaya gibidir; sağanak vurdu, onu çıplak bıraktı, source:2:264}; Allah'ın rızası için harcayanınki ise sağanak da çisenti de alsa iki kat ürün veren tepedeki bir bahçedir {source:2:265}. Sonra bir soru gelir: {ar:أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُۥ جَنَّةٌۭ مِّن نَّخِيلٍۢ وَأَعْنَابٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ, tr:e-yeveddu ehadukum en tekûne lehû cennetun min nahîlin ve a'nâbin tecrî min tahtihe'l-enhâr, gloss:biriniz, altından ırmaklar akan, hurmalık ve üzüm bağından bir bahçesi olmasını ister mi, source:2:266}; aynı ayette {ar:وَأَصَابَهُ ٱلْكِبَرُ وَلَهُۥ ذُرِّيَّةٌۭ ضُعَفَآءُ فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌۭ فِيهِ نَارٌۭ فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ, tr:ve esâbehu'l-kiberu ve lehû zurriyyetun duafâu fe-esâbehâ i'sârun fîhi nârun fahtarakat, gloss:kendisine yaşlılık çökmüş, zayıf çocukları varken, bahçeye içinde ateş olan bir kasırga isabet etsin de yansın, source:2:266}. Ayet kendi işini de söyler: {ar:كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ, tr:kezâlike yubeyyinullâhu lekumu'l-âyâti leallekum tetefekkerûn, gloss:Allah size ayetleri böyle açıklar ki düşünesiniz, source:2:266}.

[¶22] Bu bahçede kökün birkaç anlamı aynı yerde durur, ama kelime olarak yalnızca kasırga geçer. Bahçede üzüm vardır, yani sıkılacak meyve; ırmaklar ve bütün ürünler, yani gelir; sahibine yaşlılık gelmiştir, yani ömrün akşamüstü; ve bütün bunları, yerden kaldırdığını göğe diken, içinde ateş taşıyan bir rüzgâr yok eder. Bir ömür boyunca sıkılmayı bekleyen ürün, tam sahibinin yeniden ekecek gücü kalmadığı vakitte gider. İkinci ayetteki kaybın en somut resmi budur; kasırga, asrın yanında duyulduğunda zamanın biriktirdiğini bir anda savurabilen yüzüdür. Kokunun yükselişi ise aynı hareketin öteki ucunda durur: geçen birinin ardından toz değil, güzel bir iz kalabilir.

<<end of 103:1 reading, paragraphs numbered>>

p kurtulan tıkanmış biri gibi olurdum, source:"ع ص ر,B008"}; söylemediği ama duyurduğu şudur: onu tıkayan suyun kendisidir, kurtaracak yudum kalmamıştır.

[¶10] Bu imgeler ayetteki zamanın yanında duyulunca zaman bir baskı olarak görünür. Günler insanın üzerinden geçer ve ondan bir şey çıkarır: ya özü akar, bağış olur, bulut gibi yağmur bırakır, ya da kuru bir kütle, susuzluktan kurumuş bir dil kalır. İkinci ayetteki kayıp, sıkılmış olanın geride kalan yanıdır; üçüncü ayetin son kelimesi olan sabrın da bir ağaçtan sıkılan acı özün adı olması {source:"ص ب ر,B008"} bu baskıyı surenin sonuna taşır.

## Yusuf'un zindanında sıkılan üzüm ve beklenen yıl

[¶11] Kur'an sıkma fiilini bir zindanda kullanır ve onu uzun bir bekleyişin içine yerleştirir. Yusuf suçsuz olduğu belli olduktan sonra, kendisini sıkıştıranların kararıyla zindana atılır: {ar:لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ, tr:le-yescununnehû hattâ hîn, gloss:onu bir süreye kadar mutlaka zindana atacaklardı, source:12:35}. Zindan burada bir süre ile ölçülmüştür; asra da bir zaman parçası denildiğini, kelimenin alıkoymak anlamı da taşıdığını hatırlamak gerekir {source:"ع ص ر,B006"}. Bu bir bağlantıdır, kelime ortaklığı değil: Kur'an zindan için başka bir kelime kullanır. Yusuf'la birlikte zindana iki genç girer; biri rüyasını anlatır: {ar:إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, tr:innî erânî a'siru hamrâ, gloss:kendimi şarap sıkarken görüyorum, source:12:36}. Gencin sıktığı şey üzümdür, ama cümle onu çıkacak içkinin adıyla söyler: sıkma, ürününün adıyla anılır. Yusuf'un yorumu bu genç için kurtuluştur: {ar:أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًۭا, tr:emmâ ehadukumâ fe-yeskî rabbehû hamrâ, gloss:biriniz efendisine şarap sunacak, source:12:41}. Ardından gelen ayet onu kurtulacak olan diye anar: {ar:وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ, tr:ve kâle li'llezî zanne ennehû nâcin minhumâ'zkurnî inde rabbik, gloss:ikisinden kurtulacağını sandığına: beni efendinin yanında an, dedi, source:12:42}. Asrın kurtuluş yeri anlamına da {ar:العصر المنجاة, tr:el-asru'l-mencât, gloss:asr, kurtuluş yeridir, source:"ع ص ر,B005"} denmesi bu sahnede yankılanır: rüyasında sıkan, zindandan kurtulan kişidir.

[¶12] Ama aynı ayet bekleyişi de uzatır: genç Yusuf'u anmayı unutur ve {ar:فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ, tr:fe-lebise fi's-sicni bid'a sinîn, gloss:Yusuf zindanda birkaç yıl kaldı, source:12:42}. Unutan genç ancak kralın rüyası anlatıldığında hatırlar: {ar:وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ, tr:ve kâle'llezî necâ minhumâ veddekera ba'de ummeh, gloss:ikisinden kurtulmuş olan, uzun bir süre sonra hatırlayıp dedi, source:12:45}. Kralın rüyasında yedi yeşil başak ve yedi kuru başak vardır {ar:وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍۢ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍۢ, tr:ve seb'a sunbulâtin hudrin ve uhara yâbisât, gloss:yedi yeşil başak ve ötekiler kuru, source:12:43}. Yusuf'un yorumu bir zaman planıdır. Önce yedi yıl ekilecek ve ürün başağında bırakılacaktır: {ar:فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ, tr:fe-mâ hasadtum fe-zerûhu fî sunbulihî illâ kalîlen mimmâ te'kulûn, gloss:biçtiğinizi, yiyeceğiniz az bir kısım dışında başağında bırakın, source:12:47}. Araplar, başağın kabukları belirdiğinde ekin için {ar:إذا تبينت أكمام السنبل قيل قد عصر الزرع, tr:izâ tebeyyenet ekmâmu's-sunbuli kîle kad asara'z-zer', gloss:başağın kabukları belirince ekin "asara" oldu denir, source:"ع ص ر,B010"} derlerdi ve bunu korunak anlamına bağlarlardı: {ar:مأخوذ من العصر وهو الحرز أي تحرز في غلفه, tr:me'hûzun mine'l-asri ve huve'l-hirz, gloss:korunak anlamındaki asrdan alınmıştır, tane kabuğunun içinde korunur, source:"ع ص ر,B010"}. Bu bir kalıp içinde yaşayan anlamdır ve Kur'an'ın kelimesi başaktır, asr değil; ama Yusuf'un planı tam bu işi yapar: tane, kabuğunun içinde, darlık yıllarına saklanır. Sonra yedi sert yıl gelir ve saklananı yer: {ar:ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌۭ شِدَادٌۭ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ, tr:summe ye'tî min ba'di zâlike seb'un şidâdun ye'kulne mâ kaddemtum lehunne illâ kalîlen mimmâ tuhsınûn, gloss:sonra yedi çetin yıl gelir, onlar için biriktirdiğinizi yer, koruyup sakladığınız az bir kısım kalır, source:12:48}. Ve en sonunda: {ar:ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌۭ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ, tr:summe ye'tî min ba'di zâlike âmun fîhi yugâsu'n-nâsu ve fîhi ya'sirûn, gloss:sonra bir yıl gelir; o yıl insanlar imdada kavuşur ve o yıl sıkarlar, source:12:49}. Bu son fiil, topraktan ürün almak diye de anlaşılmıştır: {ar:يعصرون قال يستغلون بأرضيهم, tr:ya'sirûn, yestagıllûne bi-aradîhim, gloss:sıkarlar, yani topraklarından ürün alırlar, source:"ع ص ر,B007"}.

[¶13] Bu hikâyede kökün birbirinden uzak görünen anlamları tek bir takvime dizilir: zindanda geçen süre, kurtulacak olanın rüyasındaki sıkma, unutulup uzayan yıllar, kabuğunda saklanan tane ve sıkmanın yeniden başladığı bolluk yılı. Sıkmak burada darlığın sonunu işaret eder; sıkılacak üzüm, darlık yıllarını sabırla bekleyip saklayanların payıdır. Ayetin yemin ettiği zaman bu açıdan yalnızca tüketen bir süre değildir: içinde saklananın korunduğu ve sonunda sıkılıp akan bir süredir.

## Tutmak ve vermek

[¶14] Sıkmak bir kavrayıştır, ve kavrayış iki yöne işler: tutar ya da akıtır. Asr kelimesi tutmayı da adlandırır: {ar:العصر الحبس, tr:el-asru'l-habs, gloss:asr, alıkoymaktır, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}; birine seni ne alıkoydu diye sorulurken {ar:ما عصرك أي ما منعك, tr:mâ asarak, gloss:seni ne tuttu, ne engelledi, source:"ع ص ر,B006"} denirdi. Elinden bir şey bırakmayan, veremeyen kişi için {ar:فلان عاصر إذا كان ممسكا, tr:fulânun âsirun izâ kâne mumsikâ, gloss:eli sıkı olana âsir denir, source:"ع ص ر,B006"} derlerdi. Babanın, çocuğuna ait malı ondan tutması da bu fiille söylenir: {ar:يعتصر الوالد على ولده في ماله أي يمنعه إياه ويحبسه عنه, tr:ya'tasıru'l-vâlidu alâ veledihî fî mâlih, gloss:baba çocuğunun malını ondan esirger, alıkoyar, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}; verdiği bağıştan dönüp onu geri almak da: {ar:أعطيت فلانا عطية فاعتصرتها أي رجعت فيها, tr:a'taytu fulânen atıyyeten fa'tasartuhâ, gloss:birine bir bağış verdim, sonra ondan dönüp geri aldım, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}. Bir önceki bölümdeki cömert ise aynı kökle {source:"ع ص ر,B007"} verendi. Torba örneği bu ikiliği açıklar: sıkan el sıkıca kavrar; kavrayış sıvıyı dışarı akıtırsa bağış olur, kavrayış yalnızca tutarsa cimrilik olur. Aynı fiil hem el açıklığını hem el sıkılığını adlandırabilir, çünkü ikisi de bir şeyi avuçta sıkmaktır; fark, avuçtan bir şeyin çıkıp çıkmamasıdır.

[¶15] Tutmak her zaman kötü değildir. İlk aybaşı vaktinde evde tutulan genç kızın adı da buradan gelir: {ar:المعصر ساعة تطمث أي تحيض لأنها تحبس في البيت يجعل لها عصرا, tr:el-mu'sır, gloss:ilk aybaşı vaktindeki kız; evde tutulduğu, kendisine bir korunak yapıldığı için böyle denir, source:"ع ص ر,B009"}; kabuğunda saklanan tane de aynı korunağın içindedir {source:"ع ص ر,B010"}. Burada tutmak, bir eşikte olanı korumaktır.

[¶16] Kur'an ürünü tutmanın ne getirdiğini bir bahçe sahneleriyle anlatır. Peygamber'i yalanlayanlara, onları bir bahçenin sahipleri gibi sınadığını söyler: {ar:إِنَّا بَلَوْنَٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ, tr:innâ belevnâhum kemâ belevnâ ashâbe'l-cenneti iz aksemû le-yasrimunnehâ musbihîn, gloss:onları, sabah olunca bahçenin ürününü mutlaka devşireceklerine yemin eden bahçe sahiplerini sınadığımız gibi sınadık, source:68:17}, {ar:وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, tr:ve lâ yestesnûn, gloss:ve hiçbir istisna yapmıyorlardı, source:68:18}. Niyetleri, ürünü yoksula kapatmaktır: {ar:أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌۭ, tr:en lâ yedhulennehe'l-yevme aleykum miskîn, gloss:bugün oraya yanınıza hiçbir yoksul girmesin, source:68:24}. Onlar uyurken bahçenin üzerinden Rab'den gelen bir şey geçer {ar:فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ, tr:fe-tâfe aleyhâ tâifun min rabbike ve hum nâimûn, gloss:onlar uyurken Rabbinden bir dolaşan onun üzerinden dolaştı, source:68:19} ve bahçe kopkoyu bir yere döner {ar:فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ, tr:fe-asbahat ke's-sarîm, gloss:sabaha kesilip kararmış gibi çıktı, source:68:20}. Gördüklerinde ilk sözleri {ar:إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ, tr:innâ le-dâllûn, gloss:biz yolu şaşırmışız, source:68:26}, ardından {ar:بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ, tr:bel nahnu mahrûmûn, gloss:hayır, biz yoksun bırakılmışız, source:68:27} olur. Tutulan ürün tutanın elinde kalmamıştır. Bu bahçe sahipleri istisnasız bir yemin etmişlerdi; surenin yemini ise ikinci ayetteki genel hükmün ardından üçüncü ayetin istisnasıyla tamamlanır.

## Sığınak

[¶17] Asrın sıkıştırma anlamının karşısında, şaşırtıcı biçimde, sığınak anlamı durur. [¶11] Kur'an sıkma fiilini bir zindanda kullanır ve onu uzun bir bekleyişin içine yerleştirir. Yusuf suçsuz olduğu belli olduktan sonra, kendisini sıkıştıranların kararıyla zindana atılır: {ar:لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ, tr:le-yescununnehû hattâ hîn, gloss:onu bir süreye kadar mutlaka zindana atacaklardı, source:12:35}. Zindan burada bir süre ile ölçülmüştür; asra da bir zaman parçası denildiğini, kelimenin alıkoymak anlamı da taşıdığını hatırlamak gerekir {source:"ع ص ر,B006"}. Bu bir bağlantıdır, kelime ortaklığı değil: Kur'an zindan için başka bir kelime kullanır. Yusuf'la birlikte zindana iki genç girer; biri rüyasını anlatır: {ar:إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, tr:innî erânî a'siru hamrâ, gloss:kendimi şarap sıkarken görüyorum, source:12:36}. Gencin sıktığı şey üzümdür, ama cümle onu çıkacak içkinin adıyla söyler: sıkma, ürününün adıyla anılır. Ardından gelen ayet onu kurtulacak olan diye anar: {ar:وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ, tr:ve kâle li'llezî zanne ennehû nâcin minhumâ'zkurnî inde rabbik, gloss:ikisinden kurtulacağını sandığına: beni efendinin yanında an, dedi, source:12:42}. Yusuf'un yorumu bir zaman planıdır. Önce yedi yıl ekilecek ve ürün başağında bırakılacaktır: {ar:فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ, tr:fe-mâ hasadtum fe-zerûhu fî sunbulihî illâ kalîlen mimmâ te'kulûn, gloss:biçtiğinizi, yiyeceğiniz az bir kısım dışında başağında bırakın, source:12:47}. ## Tek kelimelik bir yemin

[¶1] Sure tek bir kelimeyle açılır: {ar:وَٱلْعَصْرِ, tr:ve'l-asr, gloss:asra andolsun, source:103:1}. Baştaki "ve" burada iki şeyi birbirine bağlayan bağlaç değil, yemin edatıdır; ardındaki isim bu yüzden esre ile okunur. Yeminin neye dair olduğu bu ayette söylenmez, bir sonraki ayete bırakılır. Birinci ayet bu yüzden bir eşik gibidir: okuyan, neyin üzerine yemin edildiğini duyar, ama hangi hükmün söyleneceğini henüz bilmez. Hüküm ikinci ayette gelir: {ar:إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ, tr:inne'l-insâne le-fî husr, gloss:insan gerçekten kayıp içindedir, source:103:2}. Yeminle öne konan şey, ardından gelecek hükmün hemen yanına yerleştirilmiştir; asrın ne olduğunu iyi duymak, kaybın nasıl bir kayıp olduğunu duymanın da yoludur.

[¶2] Kur'an başka surelerde de günün vakitleri üzerine yemin eder: {ar:وَٱلْفَجْرِ, tr:ve'l-fecr, gloss:şafağa andolsun, source:89:1}, {ar:وَٱلضُّحَىٰ, tr:ve'd-duhâ, gloss:kuşluk vaktine andolsun, source:93:1}, {ar:وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ, tr:ve'l-leyli izâ yağşâ, gloss:her şeyi örttüğünde geceye andolsun, source:92:1}, {ar:وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ, tr:ve's-subhi izâ esfer, gloss:ağardığında sabaha andolsun, source:74:34}. Bunların çoğunda vakit bir hareketle birlikte anılır: gece örttüğünde, sabah ağardığında. Asr ise yalnız gelir, hiçbir niteleme almaz; bu yalnızlık kelimenin genişliğini açık bırakır. Çünkü aynı kelime hem günün bir dilimini hem de zamanın bütününü adlandırır. Uzun zamana, çağa {ar:العصر الدهر, tr:el-asru'd-dehr, gloss:asr, uzun zaman, çağdır, source:"ع ص ر,B001"} denir; günün akşama yakın kısmına da {ar:العصر العشي, tr:el-asru'l-aşiyy, gloss:asr, akşamüstüdür, source:"ع ص ر,B001"}; o vakitte kılınan namaz da adını ondan alır: {ar:صلاة العصر, tr:salâtu'l-asr, gloss:ikindi namazı, source:"ع ص ر,B001"}. Kelimedeki belirlilik takısı bilinen bir vakti gösterir, ama hangisinin, günün ikindisinin mi, insanın içinde yaşadığı çağın mı, zamanın kendisinin mi kastedildiğini ayet söylemez. Tek kelime, okuyanı bunları birlikte duymaya bırakır.

[¶3] Türkçe bu kelimeyi ikiye bölmüştür. "Asır" bugün yüz yıl demektir, "asri" de çağdaş; günün sonu ise "ikindi" diye başka bir kelimeyle söylenir. Türkçede "asır" denince ne akşamüstünün azalan ışığı duyulur ne de aşağıda görülecek sıkma, sığınak ve kasırga. Ayetteki kelime ise saati de çağı da bir arada tutar: bir günün sonu ile bir ömrün sonu aynı adı taşır.

Akana {ar:العصارة ما سال عن العصر, tr:el-usâratu mâ sâle ani'l-asr, gloss:usâre, sıkmadan akandır, source:"ع ص ر,B002"} adı verilir; suyu sıkılarak alınmış her şeye de {ar:كل شيء عصر ماؤه فهو عصير, tr:kullu şey'in usira mâuhû fe-huve asîr, gloss:suyu sıkılmış her şey asîrdir, source:"ع ص ر,B002"} denir. Torbada kalan ise posadır {source:"ع ص ر,B002"}. Sıkma böylece bir şeyi ikiye ayırır: akıp giden öz ve geride kalan kuru kütle.

[¶8] Bu işin ürünü iyiliğin adı olmuştur. Araplar sıkılıp akan özü hayrın ve bağışın misali yaparlardı {ar:العرب تجعل العصارة والمعتصر مثلا للخير والعطاء, tr:el-arabu tec'alu'l-usârate ve'l-mu'tasare mesalen li'l-hayri ve'l-atâ', gloss:Araplar usâreyi ve sıkılan yeri hayır ve bağış için misal yaparlar, source:"ع ص ر,B007"}; cömert biri için {ar:يعصر فينا كالذي تعصر, tr:ya'siru fînâ ke'llezî ta'sir, gloss:bize senin verdiğin gibi verir, source:"ع ص ر,B007"} derlerdi, topraktan alınan gelire de {ar:العصارة الغلة, tr:el-usâratu'l-galle, gloss:usâre, üründür, source:"ع ص ر,B007"} denirdi. Sıkma göğe de taşınır. Bulutun yağmurla sıkıldığı söylenir: {ar:المعصرات السحائب تعتصر بالمطر, tr:el-mu'sırâtu's-sehâibu ta'tasıru bi'l-matar, gloss:mu'sırât, yağmurla sıkılan bulutlardır, source:"ع ص ر,B003"}, {ar:السحابة المعصر التي تتحلب بالمطر, tr:es-sehâbetu'l-mu'sır, gloss:yağmuru sağılır gibi akıtan bulut, source:"ع ص ر,B003"}; yağmura kavuşan topluluk için {ar:عصر القوم أي مطروا, tr:usira'l-kavm, gloss:topluluk yağmura kavuştu, source:"ع ص ر,B003"} denir. Kur'an bu bulutları kendi adlarıyla anar. Kıyamet haberini tartışanlara yeryüzünün düzeni sayılırken şöyle denir: {ar:وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ مَآءًۭ ثَجَّاجًۭا, tr:ve enzelnâ mine'l-mu'sırâti mâen seccâcâ, gloss:sıkılan bulutlardan şarıl şarıl su indirdik, source:78:14}, {ar:لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِۦ حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا, tr:li-nuhrice bihî habben ve nebâtâ, gloss:onunla tane ve bitki çıkaralım diye, source:78:15}, {ar:وَجَنَّٰتٍ أَلْفَافًا, tr:ve cennâtin elfâfâ, gloss:ve iç içe geçmiş bahçeler, source:78:16}. Bulutun sıkılması burada bir bereket zinciri başlatır: sıkılan bulut, tane, bitki, bahçe.

[¶9] Sıkmanın öteki ucu kuruluktur. Susuzluktan kurumuş dile {ar:المعصور اللسان اليابس عطشا, tr:el-ma'sûru'l-lisânu'l-yâbisu atşâ, gloss:ma'sûr, susuzluktan kurumuş dildir, source:"ع ص ر,B014"} denir: sıkılmış, içinde su kalmamış dil. Aynı fiil bir kurtuluş hareketini de adlandırır. Lokma boğazına takılan kişi suyu azar azar içerek onu geçirir: {ar:الاعتصار أن يغص الإنسان بالطعام فيعتصر بالماء وهو أن يشربه قليلا قليلا ليسيغه, tr:el-i'tisâru en yagassa'l-insânu bi't-taâmi fe-ya'tasıra bi'l-mâ', gloss:i'tisâr, insanın yemekle tıkanınca suyu yudum yudum içip lokmayı geçirmesidir, source:"ع ص ر,B008"}. Bir şair bu hareketi tersinden kullanmıştır: {ar:لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق كنت كالغصان بالماء اعتصاري, tr:lev bi-gayri'l-mâi halkî şarikun kuntu ke'l-gassâni bi'l-mâi'-tisârî, gloss:boğazım sudan başka bir şeyle tıkansaydı, suyla yudumlayı

turns on: Whether the unqualified word is inclusive or specifies a time of day, a prayer, a paired period, or a marked era; arguments use Arabic usage, poetry, report, context and analogous oaths.
- 103:1/q01/p1 Time or an age broadly, encompassing its changing periods and events.
  reasons: Al-Tabari declines restriction without textual proof; al-Nahhas and Elmalılı likewise allow several Arabic senses. Ibn Abbas and others identify an age; Imru al-Qays and Ibn al-Sikkit's poetry attest the usage. Farāhī and Asad distinguish fleeting ʿaṣr from dahr; Cuypers calls it a general span without further grounds. Ibn Kathir calls this the well-known view. Bint al-Shati follows al-Tabari, Ibn Qayyim and most exegetes; Kur'an Yolu finds this best suited to the sūra. Al-Razi questions treating a reported expanded wording as Qur'an because that would invalidate prayer. Elmalılı cites a poet likening unseen time's motion toward death to a ship. Al-Damghani glosses al-ʿaṣr as time or its passage; al-Suyuti includes time as a whole among the oath's possible referents.

- 103:1/q01/p3 The afternoon prayer, the middle prayer distinguished by special merit.
  reasons: Muqatil calls it the middle and best prayer. Neuwirth links prayer-time oaths to liturgical experience, though Corpus Coranicum disputes the proposed hymn tone.

  reasons: Mawardi and Qurtubi cite renewed prophethood. Razi and Elmalılı invoke the workers' parable: the final workers labor from Asr to sunset and receive double pay; compare oaths by the Prophet's place and life (90:2; 15:72). Elmalılı describes the mission, Hijra, victory, and extension of Muhammad's community to the end of time; the afternoon of human history follows earlier ages.   reasons: Muqatil calls it the middle and best prayer. # 103:1/q03 How does the opening oath work, and what does it emphasize? [وَٱلْعَصْرِ · rhetoric]
turns on: Whether wāw is explained as a conventional emphatic oath or as time's witness to the proposition.
- 103:1/q03/p1 The wāw introduces an oath whose answer affirms that humanity is in loss.
  reasons: Jishumi identifies the oath particle and its answer; Elmalılı compares 93:1. Ibn Ashur says an oath confirms the assertion and its object displays God's creation, power and knowledge. Bint al-Shati says wāw magnifies what is sworn by and moves from perceptible reality to moral truth. Corpus Coranicum notes a possible pre-Islamic seer formula, a connection not yet studied adequately. Al-Zarkashi and al-Suyuti count oath openings as the fifth of the sūra-opening modes and list fifteen such sūras; al-Suyuti further classifies al-ʿAṣr as an oath followed by a proposition about human conduct or condition, namely humanity's loss.

# 103:1/q04 Why is time or afternoon singled out for the oath? [وَٱلْعَصْرِ · interpretation]
turns on: The explanations appeal to divine signs, the day's closure, the prayer's status, the Prophet's era, historical recompense, or the value and moral use of time.
- 103:1/q04/p1 Time displays divine power and wondrous changes, so its oath invites reflection.
  reasons: Alternating nights and days, shifting light and temperature, health and illness, wealth and poverty, and other events disclose God's power (Razi, Ibn Qayyim, Tabarsi). Razi cites 25:62 and 6:13. Bursevi relates the oath to dawn, sun, moon, night, day and forenoon oaths. Ibn Ashur adds the solar-earth cycle and daily social life. Bint al-Shati cautions against loading the verse with speculative philosophy and cites 28:71–72.

# 103:1/q02 What meanings and derivations does the word ʿaṣr have in Arabic? [ٱلْعَصْرِ · meaning]
turns on: The sources distinguish its concrete pressing root, wide Arabic uses, bounded temporal force and the definite article's scope.
- 103:1/q02/p1 Its root denotes squeezing or pressing, extended to time, confinement, and the extraction of an essence.
  reasons: Jishumi describes wringing cloth, grape extract, deferred prayer, rain-bearing clouds and a rising dust column. Tabarsi applies the pressed-events image to time. Bint al-Shati adds press equipment, lineage and the hardship that presses out a person's essence; she cites 12:36, 12:49, 78:14 and 2:266. Biqai connects the sūra name to extracting the saved essence. Bint al-Shati reads human life as pressed and refined by trials, exposing its essence; she cites the root's occurrences in Yusuf's dream and harvest year and the whirlwind in al-Baqara, calls this Qur'anic form unique, and rejects al-Raghib's derivation of temporal ʿaṣr from what remains after squeezing. Her criticism of proposed links in other oaths cautions against assuming a simple analogy for this image.

turns on: Whether the oath's prayer-time association produces a hymn-like effect.

  reasons: Corpus Coranicum describes the structure; Neuwirth supports keeping the oath as an independent verse. # 103:1/q20 How is the transition from al-ʿAṣr to the next sūra recited? [* · readings]
turns on: The transmitted practice of a reader who ordinarily joins or pauses between sūras.
- 103:1/q20/p1 Some readers who generally join sūras make a brief pause at this transition.
  reasons: Ibn al-Jazari reports a special sakt among several Hamza, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, Yaʿqub and Warsh readers. He explains that separating the ending wa-tawāṣaw bi-l-ṣabr from the next opening wayl avoids a jarring joined phrase; special sakt presupposes joining elsewhere.
  holders (3 notes): NASHR
  notes: NASHR:v1p261#2/r1 NASHR:v1p261#2/r3 NASHR:v1p261#2/r6
- 103:1/q20/p2 Some readers who generally pause insert the basmala at this transition.
  reasons: Ibn al-Jazari reports this practice from Ibn Ghalbun, the Hidaya author, Makki and others; it separates the same jarring phrase, and the special basmala presupposes pausing elsewhere.
  holders (3 notes): NASHR
  notes: NASHR:v1p261#2/r2 NASHR:v1p261#2/r3 NASHR:v1p261#2/r6
- 103:1/q20/p3 Most authorities give this transition no special treatment, and joiners do not insert an untransmitted basmala.
  reasons: Ibn al-Jazari names Faris ibn Ahmad, Ibn Sufyan, Abu al-Tahir, Iraqi authorities and al-Dani among those making no distinction.   notes: NASHR:v1p261#2/r4 NASHR:v1p261#2/r5 NASHR:v1p261#2/r6
sources: NASHR = Ibn al-Jazarī, d. 833

# 103:1/q21 Where does al-ʿAṣr stand in the reported codex order of Ibn Masʿūd? [* · sciences]
- 103:1/q21/p1 It appears among the mufassal sūras after al-Fajr.
  reasons: Al-Suyuti reports this order for Ibn Masʿūd's codex.
  holders (1 notes): ITQAN(عبد الله بن مسعود)
  notes: ITQAN:v1p176/r1

# 103:1/q22 What principle determines whether the opening of al-ʿAṣr is a separate āya? [وَٱلْعَصْرِ · sciences]
turns on: Whether verse boundaries can be inferred by analogy and form or require transmitted specification.
- 103:1/q22/p1 An āya is a marked, separate unit of Qur'anic speech, understood through its boundaries or function as a sign.

# 103:2/q01 What is the grammatical answer to the oath? [إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ · grammar]
- 103:2/q01/p1 The declaration that humanity is in loss answers the oath by time.
  reasons: Jishumi identifies the oath wāw and this clause as its answer; Ibn al-Jawzi reports al-Zajjaj; Study Quran takes verses 2–3 as the answer and compares 95:5–6; Corpus Coranicum describes an opening oath followed by rebuke. Al-Suyuti classifies al-ʿAṣr as a Qur'anic oath followed by a proposition about human action or condition: humanity is in loss.
  holders (5 notes): JISHUMI; IBNJAWZI-ZAD(الزجاج); STUDYQURAN; CORPUSCORANICUM; ITQAN
  notes: JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9 IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r1 STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1 CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1 ITQAN:v4p353/r5
sources: CORPUSCORANICUM = Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments); IBNJAWZI-ZAD = Ibn al-Jawzī, d. 597; ITQAN = al-Suyūṭī, d. 911; JISHUMI = al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī, d. 494; STUDYQURAN = Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom

# 103:2/q10 How is the oath by time related to the human loss that follows? [إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ · rhetoric]
turns on: Whether the oath evokes life's finite capital, the late hour and reckoning, or time's warning events.
- 103:2/q10/p1 Time is the valuable, vanishing opportunity in which human gain or loss is determined.
  reasons: Elmalili says time contains changes, wonders, blessing, harm and the chance to act; its passing consumes life unless used for faith and reform. He says the oath honors time rather than blaming it, and its senses of restraint and bestowal evoke both loss and gain. Kuranyolu similarly says God swears by precious time; Islahi relates it to responsibility for life's blessing.
  holders (11 notes): ELMALILI; KURANYOLU-TEFSIR; ISLAHI-TADABBUR; STUDYQURAN
  notes: ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1 ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5 ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6 ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10 ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12 ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13 ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4 ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6 ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1 STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3
- 103:2/q10/p2 Late afternoon evokes the closing human era or the end of life and the reckoning of what was earned.
  reasons: Elmalili evokes creation late in the world's day, the era of Muhammad and the sorrow of returning without gain. Study Quran reads humanity in a final historical phase. Robinson relates the afternoon to merchants counting daily takings; Corpus Coranicum supports this through Q 104's contrast of wealth and damnation.
  holders (5 notes): ELMALILI; STUDYQURAN; CORPUSCORANICUM; CORPUSCORANICUM(Robinson)+
  notes: ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13 ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9 STUDYQURAN:103:2/r3 CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4 CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r5
- 103:2/q10/p3 Time's calamities and transformations warn that human loss continues to its end.
  reasons: Elmalili explains Ali's interpretive dehr recitation as recurrent changes and calamities, while another view sees time's wonders as signs of the Creator's power.
  holders (2 notes): ELMALILI
  notes: ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16 ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17
- 103:2/q10/p4 An oath-to-assertion link should be tested rather than inferred from analogy alone.
  reasons: Bint al-Shati questions proposed links elsewhere: between the greatness of night and day and differing human striving, and between the falling star (53:1) and the Prophet's freedom from error. This note offers a methodological caution, not a specific alternative account of al-ʿAsr.
  holders (1 notes): BINTSHATI-IJAZ+
  notes: BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1

Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments); ELMALILI = Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır, d. 1361; ISLAHI-TADABBUR = Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997); KURANYOLU-TEFSIR = Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş; STUDYQURAN = Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom

# 6:52/q04 What does calling upon their Lord morning and evening denote? [يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلْعَشِىِّ · interpretation]
turns on: Whether الدعاء names prescribed prayer, particular prayers, remembrance, Quran, supplication, or comprehensive worship.
- 6:52/q04/p1 The prescribed prayers, sometimes all five.
  reasons: Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Hasan, Qatada, and others say obligatory prayer; some specify congregation. Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib oppose making it post-prayer storytelling. A minority identifies dawn and afternoon specifically; Muqatil and Hasan describe two Meccan daily prayers before five were prescribed; Amr ibn Shuaib identifies the evening as isha. turns on: Whether the temporal pair is literal, exemplary of constant practice, or chosen because worship then is especially significant.
- 6:52/q05/p1 They express continual devotion across the day.

# 78:14/q02 What are the muʿṣirāt? [ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ · referent]
turns on: The immediate source of rain ('from' clouds or sky) versus winds as the means of drawing it out; some explanations turn on whether the name describes imminent rainfall, squeezing, relief, or whirlwinds.
- 78:14/q02/p1 Rain-bearing clouds, heavy with water and ready to release it.
  reasons: Al-Tabari, al-Nahhas, al-Qurtubi, and Ibn Kathir favor clouds because rain comes from them and the verse says 'from'; Ibn Kathir cites 30:48. Al-Farra, Ibn Qutayba, al-Razi, al-Zamakhshari and others liken impending rain to a girl approaching menstruation; Abu al-Najm's verse is cited by al-Tha'labi, Abu Hayyan, al-Samin and al-Alusi. Al-Azhari disputes al-Farra's precise definition: Abu Ubayd's informants say a girl has reached maturity, al-Kisa'i says approaching twenty, and Ibn al-A'rabi says the moment of menstruation, relating it to seclusion/refuge. Al-Wahidi and Bursevi compare ready grain; al-Samin notes the active form suits imminence, since otherwise a passive participle would be expected for clouds pressed by winds, and reports al-Zamakhshari's entry-into-a-state explanation. Abu Ishaq derives the name from clouds squeezing out water; al-Mubarrad says they retain and release water gradually, with 'asr also meaning refuge. Ibn Kaysan links the term to relief and 12:49; al-Samin questions the form-IV derivation. Al-Azhari prefers rain clouds over whirlwinds, which do not bring rain. Al-Biqai adds that these clouds cool the sun and enable food and drink. Ibn Kathir reports al-Tabari's preference; Islahi says water-laden and rain-producing clouds do not differ essentially. Sibawayh cites a verse about Mayya's dwellings and rain clouds, and al-Jurjānī cites a poetic line in which al-muʿṣirāt disperse rain upon a deserted site. Al-Itqān explicitly identifies the muʿṣirāt as clouds. Ibn ʿAbbās, as reported by Bint al-Shāṭiʾ, says clouds press one another so water emerges and cites al-Nābigha's poetry. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ says that two clouds are not required by this gloss; rain-heavy clouds suffice. She cites al-Rāghib's definition as rain-saturated clouds, favors it from context and Quranic usage, and traces the root to pressure that extracts liquid, comparing 12:36, 12:49, and 2:266.

- 78:14/q02/p2 Winds that squeeze, form, drive, or draw rain from clouds.
  reasons: Ibn Zayd cites 30:48 for winds raising clouds; al-Wahidi reports a rain-bringing wind, while al-Baghawi describes winds compressing clouds. Mujahid and others also describe whirlwinds or cyclonic winds. Al-Azhari, al-Tabrisi and Ibn al-Jawzi take min instrumentally as bi; al-Tabari objects that winds do not contain water, and al-Qurtubi prefers clouds as rain's immediate source. Al-Zamakhshari says winds form clouds and release moisture and cautiously reports that winds carry water from heaven. Al-Alusi says they compress clouds until rain falls. Bursevi rejects a causative derivation because winds themselves do the squeezing. Ibn Kathir cites reports from Ibn Abbas through al-Awfi and Ibn Abi Hatim. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ relates iʿṣār to the same root sense of pressure and describes it as a strong wind driving clouds, comparing 2:266.

turns on: Whether the verb is physical squeezing, a related action such as milking, an Arabic rescue or prosperity idiom, or a rain expression; cited readings, poetry, and early authorities supply the competing evidence.
- 12:49/q06/p1 They press fruit and plants for juice or oil.
  reasons: The lists vary: grapes, olives, sesame, other fruit, sugarcane, radish, oil, wine, syrup, or water (Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, Ibn Jurayj and many commentators). Al-Qurṭubī cites al-Bukhārī for Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Wāḥidī relates sesame oil, grape wine, and olive oil and points to 12:36. Al-Fārisī and al-Ṭabrisī report fourteen years without pressing oil or grapes; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān report that nothing was pressed during drought. Al-Samīn calls this the clearest sense; al-Biqāʿī says pressing expresses the transition to fertility. Al-Ṭabarī rejects the rescue derivation because Companion and Successor interpretation favors pressing; al-Wāḥidī reports al-Fārisī favoring both pressing and rescue. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ derives the root's forms from pressure exerted to extract juice, making grape pressing the concrete source of the sense.

# 78:14/q02 What are the muʿṣirāt? [ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ · referent]
turns on: The immediate source of rain ('from' clouds or sky) versus winds as the means of drawing it out; some explanations turn on whether the name describes imminent rainfall, squeezing, relief, or whirlwinds.
- 78:14/q02/p1 Rain-bearing clouds, heavy with water and ready to release it.
  reasons: Al-Tabari, al-Nahhas, al-Qurtubi, and Ibn Kathir favor clouds because rain comes from them and the verse says 'from'; Ibn Kathir cites 30:48. Al-Farra, Ibn Qutayba, al-Razi, al-Zamakhshari and others liken impending rain to a girl approaching menstruation; Abu al-Najm's verse is cited by al-Tha'labi, Abu Hayyan, al-Samin and al-Alusi. Al-Azhari disputes al-Farra's precise definition: Abu Ubayd's informants say a girl has reached maturity, al-Kisa'i says approaching twenty, and Ibn al-A'rabi says the moment of menstruation, relating it to seclusion/refuge. Al-Wahidi and Bursevi compare ready grain; al-Samin notes the active form suits imminence, since otherwise a passive participle would be expected for clouds pressed by winds, and reports al-Zamakhshari's entry-into-a-state explanation. Abu Ishaq derives the name from clouds squeezing out water; al-Mubarrad says they retain and release water gradually, with 'asr also meaning refuge. Ibn Kaysan links the term to relief and 12:49; al-Samin questions the form-IV derivation. Al-Azhari prefers rain clouds over whirlwinds, which do not bring rain. Al-Biqai adds that these clouds cool the sun and enable food and drink. Ibn Kathir reports al-Tabari's preference; Islahi says water-laden and rain-producing clouds do not differ essentially. Sibawayh cites a verse about Mayya's dwellings and rain clouds, and al-Jurjānī cites a poetic line in which al-muʿṣirāt disperse rain upon a deserted site. Al-Itqān explicitly identifies the muʿṣirāt as clouds. Ibn ʿAbbās, as reported by Bint al-Shāṭiʾ, says clouds press one another so water emerges and cites al-Nābigha's poetry. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ says that two clouds are not required by this gloss; rain-heavy clouds suffice. She cites al-Rāghib's definition as rain-saturated clouds, favors it from context and Quranic usage, and traces the root to pressure that extracts liquid, comparing 12:36, 12:49, and 2:266.

Bursevi rejects a causative derivation because winds themselves do the squeezing. Ibn Kathir cites reports from Ibn Abbas through al-Awfi and Ibn Abi Hatim. # 12:49/q06 What do people do in يَعْصِرُونَ? [يَعْصِرُونَ · meaning]
turns on: Whether the verb is physical squeezing, a related action such as milking, an Arabic rescue or prosperity idiom, or a rain expression; cited readings, poetry, and early authorities supply the competing evidence.
- 12:49/q06/p1 They press fruit and plants for juice or oil.
  reasons: The lists vary: grapes, olives, sesame, other fruit, sugarcane, radish, oil, wine, syrup, or water (Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, Ibn Jurayj and many commentators). Al-Qurṭubī cites al-Bukhārī for Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Wāḥidī relates sesame oil, grape wine, and olive oil and points to 12:36. Al-Fārisī and al-Ṭabrisī report fourteen years without pressing oil or grapes; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān report that nothing was pressed during drought. Al-Samīn calls this the clearest sense; al-Biqāʿī says pressing expresses the transition to fertility. Al-Ṭabarī rejects the rescue derivation because Companion and Successor interpretation favors pressing; al-Wāḥidī reports al-Fārisī favoring both pressing and rescue. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ derives the root's forms from pressure exerted to extract juice, making grape pressing the concrete source of the sense.

Al-Samīn calls this the clearest sense; al-Biqāʿī says pressing expresses the transition to fertility. Al-Ṭabarī rejects the rescue derivation because Companion and Successor interpretation favors pressing; al-Wāḥidī reports al-Fārisī favoring both pressing and rescue. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ derives the root's forms from pressure exerted to extract juice, making grape pressing the concrete source of the sense.

# 12:36/q21 What does 'wine' mean as the thing pressed, and how is the wording explained? [أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا · meaning]
turns on: Whether khamr directly names grapes, anticipates wine, abbreviates a construction, or names the intended product.
- 12:36/q21/p1 It means grapes in a dialect, especially Oman or Azd Oman.
  reasons: Al-Asmaʿi's Bedouin called carried grapes khamr; al-Dahhak says the Quran uses several peoples' speech. Some name Ghassan and Azd Oman, while Ibn al-Qasim says Quraysh knew it. This explains the object directly. Al-Zarkashī relays Ibn Durayd through al-Fārisī on the Azd Oman lexical usage and a view denying metaphor on that basis; al-Suyūṭī reports al-Ḍaḥḥāk's Omani gloss.
  holders (31 notes): IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB(الأصمعي); TAB-FULL(ابن عباس، الضحاك، محمد بن الحنفية); ZAJJAJ; IBNABIHATIM(الضحاك); THALABI(الأصمعي); MAWARDI-FULL(الضحاك); WAHIDI-BASIT(الأصمعي، الضحاك، الكلبي); BAGHAWI-FULL; KASHSHAF-FULL; IBNATIYYA-FULL(الأصمعي); IBNJAWZI-ZAD(الضحاك والزجاج); RAZI-FULL(أبو صالح); QURTUBI-FULL(الضحاك); NASAFI-FULL; ABUHAYYAN-FULL(المعتمر); SAMIN-DURR(المعتمر); IBNKATHIR-FULL(الضحاك); DURR-FULL(ابن عباس، الضحاك); BURHAN(قيل); ITQAN(الضحاك)
- 12:36/q21/p2 Grapes are called wine by anticipating what they will become.
  reasons: Al-Zajjaj compares naming a thing by its eventual product; al-Wahidi cites cooking bricks from clay and molasses or juice. Ibn al-Anbari and many commentators take this as the common explanation. Al-Sijistani's separate evidence notes masculine khamr among eloquent speakers. Ibn Jinnī treats wine as the grapes' effect, named in place of its cause; al-Zarkashī describes the grapes by their future wine, and al-Suyūṭī compares other things named by their future state.
  holders (25 notes): TAB-FULL; ZAJJAJ; IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB(ابن مسعود); MAWARDI-FULL; WAHIDI-BASIT(ابن الأنباري، الزجاج); BAGHAWI-FULL; KASHSHAF-FULL; IBNATIYYA-FULL; IBNJAWZI-ZAD(أكثر المفسرين وابن الأنباري); RAZI-FULL; BAYDAWI-FULL; NASAFI-FULL; ABUHAYYAN-FULL; SAMIN-DURR; BIQAI-FULL; BURSEVI; ALUSI-FULL(ابن عطية); TABATABAI; BURHAN(ابن جني); ITQAN
- 12:36/q21/p3 An omitted noun is understood: grapes intended for wine.
  reasons: Al-Zajjaj and later authors supply the missing grapes; al-Qurtubi calls it an omitted genitive relation and adds khamra/khamr/khumur inflection.
  holders (4 notes): WAHIDI-BASIT(الزجاج); IBNJAWZI-ZAD; RAZI-FULL; QURTUBI-FULL
- 12:36/q21/p4 Wine itself may be called pressed because grapes are pressed for its sake.
  reasons: Ibn Qutayba compares saying 'I pressed oil' for olives; Ibn ʿAtiyya and Abu Hayyan permit the goal of pressing as its object. Al-Alusi says this differs from the common future-product explanation. Al-Zarkashī reports Ibn ʿAzīz's proposal that the transferred usage lies in the verb aʿṣiru, meaning to extract.

# 12:36/q22 What reading says 'grapes' in place of 'wine,' and what status does it have? [خَمْرًۭا · readings]
turns on: Whether the reported substitution is recited text or explanatory wording.
- 12:36/q22/p1 Ibn Masud and Ubayy are reported to read 'I press grapes.'
  reasons: Al-Tabari and others cite Ibn Masud; Ibn ʿAtiyya and Abu Hayyan add Ubayy. Al-Durr says Ibn Masud swore the Prophet gave him this wording. The reading makes grapes explicit. The Muḥtasab preface specifically notes Ibn Jinnī's defense of Ibn ʿAbbās's ʿinaban wording.

# 12:42/q01 Who expected one prisoner to survive, and how certain was that expectation? [ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا · interpretation]
turns on: Whether ظن names Joseph's certainty or inference, or the prisoner's response to Joseph's revealed interpretation.
- 12:42/q01/p1 Joseph knew the cupbearer would survive; “thought” expresses certain knowledge or conviction.
  reasons: Al-Tabari says prophetic prediction cannot be falsely certain; Ibn Atiyya and al-Tabataba'i cite قضي الأمر; al-Tabrisi cites 69:20 and al-Alusi and al-Tabataba'i cite 2:46. Al-Biqa'i says human knowledge is modest beside God's; al-Alusi notes the imperfect prepares Joseph's request. Al-Samarra'i calls zann the highest degree of knowledge, an apprehension reaching certainty, and cites 69:20 and 2:249.
  holders (22 notes): TAB-FULL; MAWARDI-FULL(ابن شجرة); WAHIDI-BASIT(ابن عباس); BAGHAWI-FULL; IBNATIYYA-FULL; IBNJAWZI-ZAD(ابن عباس); RAZI-FULL; BAYDAWI-FULL; NASAFI-FULL; SAMIN-DURR(الزمخشري); BIQAI-FULL; ALUSI-FULL; IBNASHUR-FULL; TABATABAI; QURTUBI-FULL(جمهور المفسرين)+; SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT+; TABRISI(أكثرون، الجبائي)+; THALABI+
- 12:42/q01/p2 Joseph inferred the cupbearer's survival with ordinary, fallible conjecture.
  reasons: Qatada says dream interpretation is conjectural; al-Wahidi adds that God may confirm or annul it; al-Mawardi proposes Joseph doubted whether the prisoners told true dreams. Ibn Atiyya and Abu Hayyan object that قضي الأمر sounds decisive unless it merely ends the interpretation. Al-Razi, al-Baydawi, al-Nasafi, and al-Samin tie this to interpretation by reasoning.
  holders (20 notes): TAB-FULL(قتادة); MAWARDI-FULL(قتادة); WAHIDI-BASIT(قتادة); IBNATIYYA-FULL(قتادة); TABRISI(قتادة); IBNJAWZI-ZAD(قتادة); RAZI-FULL; QURTUBI-FULL(جمهور المفسرين); BAYDAWI-FULL; NASAFI-FULL; SAMIN-DURR(قتادة); ABUHAYYAN-FULL(الزمخشري، قتادة); BIQAI-FULL; ALUSI-FULL; DURR-FULL(قتادة); TAB-FULL-; THALABI-; IBNATIYYA-FULL-; TABATABAI-
- 12:42/q01/p3 The saved prisoner himself expected release.

# 12:42/q06 Whom did Satan cause to forget, and what was forgotten? [فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِۦ · referent]

  reasons: Ibn Ishaq and others give this reading. Abu Hayyan and al-Alusi say distraction and palace duties account for the lapse; 12:45 says the man later remembered (al-Qurtubi, al-Alusi, al-Tabataba'i, Kur'an Yolu). Ibn Kathir rejects the alternative reports as weak; al-Tabataba'i invokes Joseph's protection from Satan. Al-Zarkashi allows dhikr as a reminder or verbal noun of mentioning, with the mention attached to the lord by semantic affinity.

# 12:42/q14 How long was Joseph imprisoned, and which part of the term followed the request? [فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ · reports]
turns on: Whether biḍʿ counts the entire confinement or only the period after Joseph's request, and how competing numerical reports are assessed.

# 12:45/q08 What does بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ mean, including its reported readings? [بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ · meaning]
turns on: The transmitted vowel and consonant forms support time, forgetting, a community, or a favor; the favor's recipient is disputed.
- 12:45/q08/p1 It means after a period, usually a long span or years.
  reasons: Ibn Qutayba and Bursevi specify seven years; Ibn Abi Hatim reports Ibn Abbas, Dahhak, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid, with Dahhak leaving the term to God. Wahidi cites Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Mujahid, the majority, Ata and language scholars; its large-group sense underlies a span of time. Ibn Durustawayh requires an omitted noun, and Akhfash says ummah is formally singular but collective, with a dog-community hadith. Ibn Ashur explains a generation-length span and cites 3:110; Bursevi compares a collective of days and hours. Qurtubi mentions 11:8. Ibn Qutayba explains the period sense through the lifespan of a community and compares 11:8; Ibn Jawzi transmits the same generational analogy and reports the exegetes' reading of 12:45 and 11:8 as a period measured in years. Damghani calls it a measured period of years, and Itqan and Burhan include the time sense.

- 12:45/q08/p2 It means after forgetfulness, read with an open or light form, sometimes with hāʾ and sometimes a still mīm.
  reasons: Farra, Majaz and Ibn Qutayba report the reading; Ibn Jinni distinguishes أمه from إمة, while Thaʿlabi's Abu Ubayda cites a poem with amihat. Jishumi's Abu Ubayd also cites poetry; Nahhas gives أمه يأمه, 'to forget.' Reports attribute variants to Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Ikrima, Mujahid, Dahhak, Qatada, Zayd ibn Ali, Abu Raja, Shibl and others. Alusi rejects dismissal of the reading. Majaz records a variant wording and the explanation 'after forgetfulness'; Ibn Qutayba reports Ibn Abbas's form alongside other reciters' form and says the forgetfulness and elapsed-time meanings both apply. Burhan attributes a light-mīm reading meaning forgetfulness to Ibn Amir.

# 12:47/q09 Why leave the harvest في سنبله? [فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ · interpretation]
- 12:47/q09/p1 Storing unthreshed grain in its ear preserves it longer, especially from insects and spoilage.
  reasons: Muqātil and Ibn ʿAbbās name weevils or pests; al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Baghawī, al-Kashshāf, al-Qurṭubī and many later commentators give preservation as the purpose. Ibn Zayd says grain still in its ear is not eaten. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān say Egyptian wheat otherwise will not last two years and advise using older stores first. Al-Ṭabrisī reports that insects avoid grain in its ear. Bursevī and al-Ālūsī suggest the dream's green ears prompted the method; Iṣlāḥī specifies termites. The report of al-Ṣādiq prescribes seven years in the ears.

# 12:45/q08 What does بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ mean, including its reported readings? [بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ · meaning]
turns on: The transmitted vowel and consonant forms support time, forgetting, a community, or a favor; the favor's recipient is disputed.
- 12:45/q08/p1 It means after a period, usually a long span or years.
  reasons: Ibn Qutayba and Bursevi specify seven years; Ibn Abi Hatim reports Ibn Abbas, Dahhak, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid, with Dahhak leaving the term to God. Wahidi cites Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Mujahid, the majority, Ata and language scholars; its large-group sense underlies a span of time. Ibn Durustawayh requires an omitted noun, and Akhfash says ummah is formally singular but collective, with a dog-community hadith. Ibn Ashur explains a generation-length span and cites 3:110; Bursevi compares a collective of days and hours. Qurtubi mentions 11:8. Ibn Qutayba explains the period sense through the lifespan of a community and compares 11:8; Ibn Jawzi transmits the same generational analogy and reports the exegetes' reading of 12:45 and 11:8 as a period measured in years. Damghani calls it a measured period of years, and Itqan and Burhan include the time sense.

# 12:47/q09 Why leave the harvest في سنبله? [فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ · interpretation]
- 12:47/q09/p1 Storing unthreshed grain in its ear preserves it longer, especially from insects and spoilage.
  reasons: Muqātil and Ibn ʿAbbās name weevils or pests; al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Baghawī, al-Kashshāf, al-Qurṭubī and many later commentators give preservation as the purpose. Ibn Zayd says grain still in its ear is not eaten. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān say Egyptian wheat otherwise will not last two years and advise using older stores first. Al-Ṭabrisī reports that insects avoid grain in its ear. Bursevī and al-Ālūsī suggest the dream's green ears prompted the method; Iṣlāḥī specifies termites. The report of al-Ṣādiq prescribes seven years in the ears.

# 12:48/q13 What does tuḥṣinūn mean? [تُحْصِنُونَ · meaning]
- 12:48/q13/p1 It means to protect, secure, save or store provisions.
  reasons: Ibn Qutayba, Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Abū ʿUbayda and other exegetes give these close glosses. Al-Ṭabarī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Ṭabrisī, Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ālūsī explain iḥṣān through a protected place, enclosure or fortress. Al-Māwardī specifies protected storehouses. # 68:18/q02 What exception did the owners fail to make? [يَسْتَثْنُونَ · interpretation]
turns on: Whether istithnāʾ qualifies the vow by God's will, excludes the poor's share, means reversal of resolve, or names a tasbīḥ formula; Bint al-Shāṭiʾ and Islahi contest the verbal-qualification reading on the story and the construction.
- 68:18/q02/p1 They did not qualify their oath or plan by God's will, such as saying 'if God wills.'
  reasons: Muqātil, al-Ṭabarī, al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Baghawī, al-Qurṭubī, and others give the formula in shāʾ Allāh. Mujāhid, reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān, says they resolved as if they controlled the outcome; Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī follows him. Al-Rāzī and Kur'an Yolu call this the majority view, while Islahi reports the exegetes as unanimous but rejects it. Al-Biqāʿī includes any other phrase returning the matter to God's will. Elmalılı includes conditions such as reaching morning safely or suffering no accident, which their confidence overlooked. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads the omission as reliance on themselves and outward causes. Al-Farrāʾ takes the later call to tasbīḥ as an instruction to qualify by in shāʾ Allāh, citing 18:24. Nāḥḥās says an unqualified intended action can be thwarted, making the speaker a liar. Ibn Kathīr says there was no exception in their oath, without specifying a formula.

# 68:18/q02 What exception did the owners fail to make? [يَسْتَثْنُونَ · interpretation]
turns on: Whether istithnāʾ qualifies the vow by God's will, excludes the poor's share, means reversal of resolve, or names a tasbīḥ formula; Bint al-Shāṭiʾ and Islahi contest the verbal-qualification reading on the story and the construction.
- 68:18/q02/p1 They did not qualify their oath or plan by God's will, such as saying 'if God wills.'
  reasons: Muqātil, al-Ṭabarī, al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Baghawī, al-Qurṭubī, and others give the formula in shāʾ Allāh. Mujāhid, reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān, says they resolved as if they controlled the outcome; Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī follows him. Al-Rāzī and Kur'an Yolu call this the majority view, while Islahi reports the exegetes as unanimous but rejects it. Al-Biqāʿī includes any other phrase returning the matter to God's will. Elmalılı includes conditions such as reaching morning safely or suffering no accident, which their confidence overlooked. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads the omission as reliance on themselves and outward causes. Al-Farrāʾ takes the later call to tasbīḥ as an instruction to qualify by in shāʾ Allāh, citing 18:24. Nāḥḥās says an unqualified intended action can be thwarted, making the speaker a liar. Ibn Kathīr says there was no exception in their oath, without specifying a formula.

# 68:20/q02 What does كالصريم liken the ruined garden to? [كَٱلصَّرِيمِ · interpretation]
turns on: Which attested sense or referent of ṣarīm supplies the simile: darkness, a cut or barren state, dawn/day, ashes, sand, the named place, or the unusual gold gloss; the notes also differ over whether the trees themselves or only their fruit were removed.
- 68:20/q02/p1 A black, dark night: the burned garden was blackened.
  reasons: Ibn Qutayba, al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj and others tie the color to burning. Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ specifies the moonless last night of a month. Al-Thaʿlabī and al-Qurṭubī cite a poem about a long dark night that dawn does not clear; al-Ṭabarī also cites poetry. Shammar and others say night and day are both ṣarīm because each separates from the other. Another derivation makes night ṣarīm because darkness stops movement or sight; al-Wāḥidī notes that this fails to explain the day usage, and al-Qushayrī objects to it. Qatāda's report says God's command came at night; Qaṭr ibn Maymūn agrees. Some authors present this alongside other possible comparisons. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ cites al-Nābigha's use of the related aṣrām in a dark-night comparison and reports Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī's citation of Zuhayr as another witness for the night sense. She reports al-Rāghib's alternative image of trees blackened as though burned.

# 68:20/q02 What does كالصريم liken the ruined garden to? [كَٱلصَّرِيمِ · interpretation]
turns on: Which attested sense or referent of ṣarīm supplies the simile: darkness, a cut or barren state, dawn/day, ashes, sand, the named place, or the unusual gold gloss; the notes also differ over whether the trees themselves or only their fruit were removed.
- 68:20/q02/p1 A black, dark night: the burned garden was blackened.
  reasons: Ibn Qutayba, al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj and others tie the color to burning. Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ specifies the moonless last night of a month. Al-Thaʿlabī and al-Qurṭubī cite a poem about a long dark night that dawn does not clear; al-Ṭabarī also cites poetry. Shammar and others say night and day are both ṣarīm because each separates from the other. Another derivation makes night ṣarīm because darkness stops movement or sight; al-Wāḥidī notes that this fails to explain the day usage, and al-Qushayrī objects to it. Qatāda's report says God's command came at night; Qaṭr ibn Maymūn agrees. Some authors present this alongside other possible comparisons. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ cites al-Nābigha's use of the related aṣrām in a dark-night comparison and reports Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī's citation of Zuhayr as another witness for the night sense. She reports al-Rāghib's alternative image of trees blackened as though burned.

# 68:26/q05 What did they mean by 'We are astray'? [إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ · interpretation]
turns on: Whether the destroyed orchard made them think they had taken a wrong road, or they already recognized moral error; the moral readings differ over excluding the poor, straying from truth, and ingratitude.
- 68:26/q05/p1 They thought they had lost the road and arrived somewhere other than their garden.
  reasons: Muqatil, Qatada as reported by Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari, al-Jishumi, al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan and al-Alusi, and Ibn Abbas as reported by Ibn Kathir and al-Durr give the wrong-road sense. Al-Farra and al-Tabari say another brother recognized the garden. Al-Zajjaj, al-Nahhas, al-Baghawi, Ibn Atiyya, Ibn al-Jawzi, al-Razi, al-Qurtubi and al-Nasafi connect their mistake to its burned, blackened or ruined condition. Al-Mawardi calls it bare; al-Biqa'i says there was no trace of crop or fruit and it no longer resembled their orchard. Al-Baydawi and al-Islahi stress their initial failure to recognize it. Al-Baghawi adds that they had denied the poor and omitted the exception; Ibn Atiyya and al-Zajjaj say they later recognized God's affliction, and al-Razi relates the loss to their miserly resolve. Elmalili says the deprivation exceeded what they had planned for the poor and led to despair of present and future benefit. Ibn Ashur says بل in the next verse corrects their mistaken identification of the site. Al-Tabatabai reports this view but adopts the moral reading; the Study Quran reports it as an alternative and also uses it in its allusion to Muhammad's opponents. Al-Damghani explicitly glosses ḍāllūn here as the garden owners having taken the wrong way to it.

- 68:26/q05/p2 They realized that trying to exclude the poor was a moral error and had brought punishment or loss upon them.
  reasons: Al-Jishumi reports a reading that they strayed by withholding the poor's due. Al-Razi says they expected to profit from barring the poor but discovered that they themselves were deprived. Al-Qurtubi says they recognized their wrongful dawn plan and the destruction as punishment. Abu Hayyan says their treachery rebounded on them. Al-Tabatabai says they had strayed from right conduct in trying to harvest while excluding the poor and then acknowledged the lost crop. Al-Alusi reports this interpretation but finds it unpersuasive.

# 68:26/q07 How did their next words correct this first statement? [لَضَآلُّونَ · links]
turns on: Whether the first words mistook the garden's location or confessed their wrong plan, and thus what the next declaration corrects.
- 68:26/q07/p1 After initially mistaking the ruined garden for another place, they recognized it and said that they had been deprived of its produce and blessing.
  reasons: Al-Farra and al-Tabari describe a brother recognizing the garden. Qatada as reported by Abd al-Razzaq and Abu Hayyan, and Ibn Abbas as reported by Ibn Kathir, give the progression from wrong path to deprivation. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn al-Jawzi say they recognized punishment; al-Baghawi attributes it to denying the poor and omitting the exception. Ibn Atiyya specifies lost yield and blessing, while al-Razi says their miserly resolve brought the loss. Al-Nasafi says they recognized the garden after looking closely. Elmalili says they found deprivation greater than they intended for the poor, with despair of present and future benefit. Ibn Ashur says بل corrects the location mistake: this was their garden, destroyed and stripped of produce. Al-Islahi says they soon realized their prized possession was gone.

# 68:27/q01 What earlier sense of being lost does 'but' correct? [بَلْ · interpretation]
turns on: Whether the earlier claim of being lost concerned the road to an unrecognizable garden or their conduct and mistaken expectation about the harvest.
- 68:27/q01/p1 They initially thought they had lost the road, then recognized the ruined garden.
  reasons: Al-Tabari says some brothers thought they had lost the way until another identified their garden. Al-Wahidi, citing Ibn Abbas, al-Baghawi, Ibn Atiyya, al-Razi, and Islahi say the burned or devastated orchard was unrecognizable at first. Al-Nahhas reports that one who recognized it corrected the mistake. Abu Hayyan, reporting Qatada, says they thought they had taken the wrong road until they saw that punishment had destroyed its bounty. turns on: Whether the destroyed orchard made them think they had taken a wrong road, or they already recognized moral error; the moral readings differ over excluding the poor, straying from truth, and ingratitude.
- 68:26/q05/p1 They thought they had lost the road and arrived somewhere other than their garden.
  reasons: Muqatil, Qatada as reported by Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari, al-Jishumi, al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan and al-Alusi, and Ibn Abbas as reported by Ibn Kathir and al-Durr give the wrong-road sense. Al-Farra and al-Tabari say another brother recognized the garden. Al-Zajjaj, al-Nahhas, al-Baghawi, Ibn Atiyya, Ibn al-Jawzi, al-Razi, al-Qurtubi and al-Nasafi connect their mistake to its burned, blackened or ruined condition. Al-Mawardi calls it bare; al-Biqa'i says there was no trace of crop or fruit and it no longer resembled their orchard. Al-Baydawi and al-Islahi stress their initial failure to recognize it. Al-Baghawi adds that they had denied the poor and omitted the exception; Ibn Atiyya and al-Zajjaj say they later recognized God's affliction, and al-Razi relates the loss to their miserly resolve. Elmalili says the deprivation exceeded what they had planned for the poor and led to despair of present and future benefit. Ibn Ashur says بل in the next verse corrects their mistaken identification of the site. Al-Tabatabai reports this view but adopts the moral reading; the Study Quran reports it as an alternative and also uses it in its allusion to Muhammad's opponents. Al-Damghani explicitly glosses ḍāllūn here as the garden owners having taken the wrong way to it.

# 18:25/q01 Who states the three hundred and nine year duration? [وَلَبِثُوا۟ ثَلَٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍۢ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًۭا · interpretation]
turns on: Whether the clause continues earlier quoted claims or resumes God's narrative; the variant with 'they said' and the force of 18:26 are disputed.
- 18:25/q01/p1 God states the sleepers' true duration.
  reasons: Mujāhid and Ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr take the count literally. Al-Ṭabarī says unmarked quotation needs proof; al-Zajjāj calls the number a stronger sign. Al-Baghawī says God's subsequent claim to know best confirms disclosed knowledge. Al-Rāzī cites the intervening ban on dispute; al-Ṭabrisī says an unmarked quotation would leave the proof of divine power incomplete. Ibn Kathīr says the People of the Book gave 300 solar years without the nine and the Ibn Masʿūd report is anomalous with disconnected transmission. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī appeals to passage structure and says their reported figure was 200 or less. # 2:266/q19 What is an i'sar? [إِعْصَارٌۭ · meaning]
turns on: Whether the word itself is a general rotating wind, a hot samum, or a cold blast.
- 2:266/q19/p1 A fierce, rotating wind or whirlwind rising like a column, often lifting dust.
  reasons: Al-Tabari gives its plural a'asir and cites Yazid ibn Mufarrigh; al-Zajjaj calls it zawba'a and cites an unnamed poet. Al-Thalabi cites al-Kumayt and Yazid ibn al-Muqri; Ibn al-Jawzi, al-Razi, al-Tabrisi, al-Samin and Ibn Abbas in al-Durr cite poetry or the wind proverb. Damghani says the fierce wind can be cold or hot. Jishumi describes its column rising from ground to sky, or a wind that raises clouds. Al-Itqan cites an anonymous poetic line and gives the singular-plural pair isar/aasir. Bint al-Shati cites Ibn Abbas's fierce-wind gloss and poem, al-Jawhari's dust-pillar or thundercloud, al-Tabari's comparable gloss and al-Raghib's dust-stirring wind; she finds the severe-wind reading suited to the root.

# 2:266/q19 What is an i'sar? [إِعْصَارٌۭ · meaning]
turns on: Whether the word itself is a general rotating wind, a hot samum, or a cold blast.
- 2:266/q19/p1 A fierce, rotating wind or whirlwind rising like a column, often lifting dust.
  reasons: Al-Tabari gives its plural a'asir and cites Yazid ibn Mufarrigh; al-Zajjaj calls it zawba'a and cites an unnamed poet. Al-Thalabi cites al-Kumayt and Yazid ibn al-Muqri; Ibn al-Jawzi, al-Razi, al-Tabrisi, al-Samin and Ibn Abbas in al-Durr cite poetry or the wind proverb. Al-Jawhari adds umm zawba'a and says the name also belongs to a jinn chief. Al-Alusi describes colliding air currents, possible upward or downward motion and force enough to uproot trees or snatch boats. Al-Tabatabai describes a twisting dust column between earth and sky. Damghani says the fierce wind can be cold or hot. Jishumi describes its column rising from ground to sky, or a wind that raises clouds. Al-Itqan cites an anonymous poetic line and gives the singular-plural pair isar/aasir. Bint al-Shati cites Ibn Abbas's fierce-wind gloss and poem, al-Jawhari's dust-pillar or thundercloud, al-Tabari's comparable gloss and al-Raghib's dust-stirring wind; she finds the severe-wind reading suited to the root.

# 2:266/q20 Why is the whirlwind called i'sar? [إِعْصَارٌۭ · meaning]
turns on: Which observed squeezing or twisting motivates the word; Ibn Atiyya and al-Qurtubi disagree about the cloth derivation.
- 2:266/q20/p1 Its coiling motion resembles cloth being wrung.
  reasons: Al-Mawardi cites a poem; al-Mahdawi gives the derivation in Ibn Atiyya and al-Qurtubi. Ibn Atiyya calls it weak, while al-Qurtubi endorses it as observable; al-Samin, al-Alusi and al-Tabatabai also mention twisting cloth.

  reasons: Ibn Atiyya cites the wind proverb and relates mu'sirat either to pregnant rain clouds or clouds compressed by winds; he reports al-Anbari and Ibn Sida's alternatives, the latter taking mu'sirat as winds. Al-Qurtubi repeats the derivations. Abu Hayyan describes a hot cloud-compressing wind; al-Harali links the name to squeezing hidden contents.   reasons: Qatada, reported by Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir and al-Suyuti, says the worldly life shrinks when the Hereafter is seen. # 79:46/q11 How does this closing comparison answer the earlier question about the Hour? [* · links]
turns on: Whether the preceding question is treated as a request for its unknown date, an impatient taunt, or a warning whose fulfillment will seem near; the reports differ on asking versus mentioning it.
- 79:46/q11/p1 It confirms the warning: the Hour will arrive swiftly and the Prophet's task is warning, while God knows its time.
  reasons: Alusi prefers a short stay after the warning or threat and says the sentence may be circumstantial or independent. Islahi says timing demands should not trouble the Prophet. Alusi rejects construing 79:43 as a substitute for their question or a quotation of it, because 79:44 directly assigns knowledge of the endpoint to God; Ibn Jurayj, reported by al-Suyuti, also glosses that endpoint as God's knowledge.
  holders (5 notes): ALUSI-FULL; DURR-FULL(ابن جرير); ISLAHI-TADABBUR; ALUSI-FULL+
  notes: ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1 ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5 ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6 DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6 ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4
- 79:46/q11/p2 It rebuts disbelievers who mockingly or impatiently demand to know when the Hour will come.
  reasons: Alusi ties the rebuke to 79:42 and prefers an interval after the warning. Study Quran says the final verses answer taunts over the Prophet's ignorance of the date.
  holders (3 notes): ALUSI-FULL; STUDYQURAN; ALUSI-FULL+
  notes: ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1 ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5 STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10
- 79:46/q11/p3 Earlier questions about the Hour ended with revelation assigning its timing to God.
  reasons: Aisha reports that the Prophet was repeatedly asked until 79:43–44 came and then stopped asking; al-Hakim authenticated this report. Tariq ibn Shihab instead reports that he often mentioned the Hour, then stopped mentioning it after those verses. Aisha also reports the Prophet telling visiting Bedouins that if their youngest lived a century their own Hour would have come.

# 35:37/q11 What does نُعَمِّرْكُم contribute? [نُعَمِّرْكُم · meaning]
- 35:37/q11/p1 God prolonged their worldly life enough for reflection and amendment.

# 79:46/q11 How does this closing comparison answer the earlier question about the Hour? [* · links]
turns on: Whether the preceding question is treated as a request for its unknown date, an impatient taunt, or a warning whose fulfillment will seem near; the reports differ on asking versus mentioning it.
- 79:46/q11/p1 It confirms the warning: the Hour will arrive swiftly and the Prophet's task is warning, while God knows its time.
  reasons: Alusi prefers a short stay after the warning or threat and says the sentence may be circumstantial or independent. Islahi says timing demands should not trouble the Prophet. Alusi rejects construing 79:43 as a substitute for their question or a quotation of it, because 79:44 directly assigns knowledge of the endpoint to God; Ibn Jurayj, reported by al-Suyuti, also glosses that endpoint as God's knowledge.
  holders (5 notes): ALUSI-FULL; DURR-FULL(ابن جرير); ISLAHI-TADABBUR; ALUSI-FULL+

- 79:46/q11/p2 It rebuts disbelievers who mockingly or impatiently demand to know when the Hour will come.
  reasons: Alusi ties the rebuke to 79:42 and prefers an interval after the warning. Study Quran says the final verses answer taunts over the Prophet's ignorance of the date.

- 79:46/q11/p3 Earlier questions about the Hour ended with revelation assigning its timing to God.
  reasons: Aisha reports that the Prophet was repeatedly asked until 79:43–44 came and then stopped asking; al-Hakim authenticated this report. Tariq ibn Shihab instead reports that he often mentioned the Hour, then stopped mentioning it after those verses. Aisha also reports the Prophet telling visiting Bedouins that if their youngest lived a century their own Hour would have come.

# 35:37/q11 What does نُعَمِّرْكُم contribute? [نُعَمِّرْكُم · meaning]
- 35:37/q11/p1 God prolonged their worldly life enough for reflection and amendment.
  reasons: Ibn ʿĀshūr defines taʿmīr as prolonging life, citing 2:96 and 35:11; al-Bursawī says reflection is opportunity to consider one's condition and amend it; al-Jishumī contrasts this worldly opportunity with its absence after death. Al-Bāqillānī invokes this verse to emphasize the long respite given to those challenged by the Qur'an before their failure to respond.

# 89:1/q03 What does al-fajr designate in the oath? [ٱلْفَجْرِ · referent]
turns on: Whether the noun denotes daily dawn, a whole day or prayer, a particular date or place, or a bursting spring or other emergence.
- 89:1/q03/p1 The familiar dawn occurring every day, taken generally.
  reasons: Ibn Abbas locates it in the east; al-Qurazi extends it daily until the world's end. Razi's Ibn Abbas report includes true and false dawn and says light ends night, sends creatures to provision and pictures resurrection (74:34; 81:18; 6:96). Alusi especially favors true dawn for its prayer and fasting role. Abu Hayyan, Ibn Ashur and Tabatabai prefer generic dawn; Ibn Ashur cites its coordination with night. Elmalili calls it the joyful move into light (81:18). Bint al-Shati uses 2:187 against extending it to the whole day; Muhammad Abduh likewise treats dawn and the ten nights generically. Baydawi compares 81:18 and Nasafi 74:34. Al-Suyuti identifies the oath's dawn as the beginning of the day.
